title: Aphelion curation reset and admin pass
content:
Aphelion has moved out of its early "live image wall" phase and into the first real curation checkpoint for the planned trading-card collection system. This pass was less about visual polish and more about getting the foundations right: use the real Keep library, choose the right database layer, and build an admin workflow that can actually support thousands of images instead of just demonstrating the idea.

The most important change was strategic. The earlier Antigravity direction was still useful conceptually, but it tried to move too quickly toward card logic before runtime, storage, and queue structure were stable. This pass reset the order of operations into something more durable: data model first, curation interface second, packs later, and user systems last.

What worked in this checkpoint:

  • MySQL-backed curation layer: Aphelion now has a real card metadata store for identity fields, rarity, review status, edition size, series, and controlled attribute assignment.
  • Runtime fixes that unlocked the admin page: the Keep image root is now parsed correctly from the UNC share, laptop dev no longer depends on E:\aphelion paths for local logs, and the admin catalog SQL query was corrected so the card list can load successfully.
  • Real admin curation surface: the app now has a working admin queue, selected-image preview, editable card identity panel, quick attributes, and CRUD tools for attribute and series libraries.
  • Folder-aware queue filtering: because the image library was already grouped into thousand-image ranges, Aphelion now derives a folder tree from folderPath and can filter the queue by batch instead of forcing all ~9,170 items into one flat list.

What did not work, and why:

  • Flat queueing: showing every card at once ignored the real library structure and was not usable for curation.
  • Over-escaped UNC env paths: Windows path normalization turned the shared image root into an invalid local path, which looked like a catalog failure until the server was tested one layer at a time.
  • Machine-specific fallback paths: dev defaults assuming server-only drive locations created new failures after the image issue itself had already been solved.
  • Layout experiments before workflow confidence: both the inline folder panel and the later slide-out folder browser solved part of the width problem, but neither matched the preferred editing composition, so the page was rolled back to the earlier block arrangement while keeping the new folder logic.

This is a meaningful reset point for Aphelion. The app now has a real curation foundation, clearer logic about what comes next, and a more honest understanding of what needs to be stable before packs and user-facing collection systems are worth building.
